summary: Jens Augspurger works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London (PhD until 2026), where he was attested in 2018, later serving as lecturer at IU International University (2022–2026) and at University of Mannheim (2026).

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held professorships at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (around 2000) and the University of Oslo (2003).

Jens Peter Laut works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, serving at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2021) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008).

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Vienna and Bonn (PhD 1993–1999 under Josef Simon), held posts at Bonn, Munich, and Bayreuth, and became professor at the University of Bern around 2009.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Munich and Göttingen, later holding professorships at the Free University of Berlin (~1995–1999), Humboldt University (1995–2001), and the University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld was a scholar of Chinese art history and sinology. Educated at Stanford and Oregon, he served as chair of art history at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and as Tang Professor at Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jervoise Athelstane Baines was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Rugby School, Trinity College, Cambridge (~1866–1869), and Trinity College Dublin, and served as a governor of the London School of Economics in 1901.

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a Polish linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He became head of its Department of General and Comparative Linguistics in 1969, professor (1977–1991), and a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1998).

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was an Indo-European linguist and Indologist. After studies in Vienna, Lviv (PhD 1921–1923), and Paris, he served as professor at the University of Lviv (1926–1946), University of Breslau (1946–1948), and Jagiellonian University (1948–1965).
Jessica Patey is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She is a PhD candidate studying and holding a post at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Jessica X. Zu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned PhDs from Pennsylvania State University (1997–2003) and Princeton University (2013–2020), and became an associate professor at the University of Southern California in 2026.

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After degrees at SOAS, Panthéon-Sorbonne, École du Louvre, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and Sorbonne University, she held post-doctoral (2014–2016), junior professor (2019), and professor (2025) posts at Ruhr University Bochum.
Jesung Woo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2001–2003).
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A student of Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007), Flick held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He was a disciple of Weijue Shi and succeeded him in 2005.

Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Renshan Yang (~1904–1911). He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head from around 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Educated at Nankai and Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Tu Weiming, he held a professorship at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a research post at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang was active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He was a disciple of Gongga Rinpoche and is listed as a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).
